description: Gold cases for attribute-merge-prompt.md (THE INTERCHANGEABILITY TEST, searcher-tolerance basis per owner rulings 2026-08-30). Every contested boundary is pinned by a REAL case on BOTH sides (prompt philosophy canon). Rulings documented in plans/attribute-merge-system.md and plans/sameness-court-report.md.

cases.why: The owner's founding example: pure spelling variants of one word must fold.
Slang praise-strength tier of the same quality — the aspect-praise canon stores both as great atmosphere.
Second slang tier — the fragmentation the owner measured (4 live twins of one claim).
Different words, one property: the cross-word half of the atmosphere family (no shared token — the case string similarity provably misses).
THE STRENGTH-TIER RULING: good/great are one claim (good value = great value precedent); a diner never runs separate searches for them.
Colloquial synonym across word families (vibe = atmosphere).
THE AFFORDABLE RULING (ideal-spec value canon): affordable IS the value token; cheap makes the same claim and folds in.
Ideal spec verbatim: 'good value' wording folds into the single affordable entity.
Item-side spelling variant (hyphenation) — the lane covers both vocabularies.
Item-side different words, one claim: portion generosity.
A specific quality is NOT a strength tier of a generic one — a romantic searcher is not satisfied by every great-atmosphere place.
Polarity is absolute (value canon): opposite value claims never merge.
A measured step a diner picks on purpose — unlike praise tiers, positions on a descriptive axis stay separate.
Opposite values of one axis — the classic embedding-close, meaning-opposite pair the judge exists to separate.
A narrower filter people seek on purpose: every rooftop is outdoor, but a rooftop searcher is not satisfied by generic outdoor seating.
Item-side opposite values sharing an axis (crust thickness).
A shared surface word spanning two different properties — judge the claim, not the word.
Cozy is a particular kind of atmosphere, not an amount of it — same law as romantic.
